title: Troubleshooting ACLs: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: Imagine a bouncer working from a bad guest list. The wrong people get in, or good ones get turned away. Let's learn to check the list.

lines.t: The bouncer has a bad list

scenes.heading: Reading the list
scenes.narration: Most ACL problems come from a few simple causes. Entries are read top down, and the first match wins. Every list ends with an invisible deny. In a wildcard mask, zero means match and one means ignore. And a list does nothing until you apply it with in or out.

scenes.heading: Check commands
scenes.narration: Three commands find most problems. Look at the match counters. See which list is applied, and where. And review the order of entries.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three traps. A list of only permits still blocks the rest. That's a wildcard, not a mask. You must always choose a direction.

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva ACL troubleshooting lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Order matters, and the first match wins. Don't forget the implicit deny. Use show access lists to check the counters. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva ACL troubleshooting lab.
